Sarah — thanks for the clear list and the tight timeline. I attached a short PDF that lays out our canonical measurement definitions; below are the highlights so your committee can get an immediate answer. We can also do a 30-minute walkthrough if that helps.

Quick answers (high level):
- Availability: % of successful API token-authenticated requests over a rolling 30-day window, measured at 1-minute granularity from our edge gateways. Success = 2xx response and completion of server-side token processing.
- p95 latency: measured at our edge ingress after TLS termination, capturing total server processing time (ms) per request over a 1-minute collection cadence; p95 is computed over the 30-day rolling window used for reporting. For short-running bursts we also compute 5m/1h percentiles for operational alerting.
- Regional incidents: we compute both global and per-region SLOs. If a region experiences a sustained degradation, the affected-region SLO is reduced; global SLA calculations use weighted aggregation by request volume. Incident windows are aligned to when customers see degraded responses (not just intra-cluster retries).
- Alerts/differentiation: customer-facing alerts (dashboard badges + email) kick at sustained p95 > 1500ms for >5m, or availability < 99.5% over a 10m sliding window. Internal ops alerts are more aggressive (p95 > 800ms, availability < 99.9%).
- Customer access: we can provide read-only Grafana views scoped to your org, 90-day raw-export on request (CSV/Parquet), and a daily aggregate metrics push to an S3 bucket if desired.
- Maintenance/exception policy: planned maintenance >5m is excluded from SLA if notified 72 hours in advance and scheduled during agreed windows; emergency maintenance is assessed case-by-case and documented in the incident record.

I'll follow up with a short tailored exhibit answering your numbered items in the format your packet expects.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: SLO measurement & telemetry access for procurement packet (Horizon)

Hi Sarah / Tim / Procurement team,

Thanks again — attached is a concise exhibit that maps directly to your numbered list plus a short schedule for onboarding dashboard access. Highlights and answers:

1) SLO definitions and windows
- Availability: measured as percentage of successful, authenticated API responses (2xx) over a rolling 30-day window. Measurements are computed at 1-minute granularity from edge ingress. Reported availability thresholds: Standard SLA = 99.9% (monthly), Business SLA options available for Dedicated customers.
- Latency (p95): p95 computed over the same rolling 30-day window at 1-minute aggregation. Operational percentiles (p50/p95/p99) are available at 5m and 1h aggregation for alerting.

2) Regional handling
- We maintain both global and per-region SLOs. When a single region degrades, affected-region SLOs are used for local impact assessment; global SLA uses volume-weighted aggregation. We explicitly exclude failover retries from availability calculations where retries result in successful completion within our configured retry policy.

3) Alerts and thresholds
- Customer-facing thresholds: availability < 99.5% over a 10m sliding window; sustained p95 > 1500ms for >5m. These trigger dashboard incident badges, email notifications to configured contacts, and a follow-up incident summary.
- Internal ops: more sensitive thresholds (p95 > 800ms, availability < 99.9%) that feed into our on-call routing and automated remediation runbooks.

4) Customer visibility & exports
- We can grant read-only Grafana with scoped dashboards (link below) and a time-limited API token for metric exports. We provide on-request raw exports for 30/90/365 day windows in CSV or Parquet. Standard provisioning timeline: dashboard access within 48 hours of onboarding; raw export delivery within 72 hours of request.
- Demo / onboarding link (read-only preview): https://grafana.redwood-inference.com/d/abcd123/horizon-view?orgId=1

5) Maintenance & exceptions
- Planned maintenance: excluded when notified 72+ hours in advance and scheduled within agreed maintenance windows. We propose a standard cap of 4 hours planned maintenance per calendar quarter; this is negotiable for enterprise agreements.
- Emergency maintenance: assessed case-by-case; significant events documented in post-incident reports and eligible for service credits per the SLA schedule.

Attachments: slo-measurement-exhibit.pdf (answers mapped to your exact procurement checklist).

If helpful, we can remove the quarterly cap language and replace with "reasonable efforts" language — legal suggested keeping a numeric cap to reduce ambiguity. Happy to join a short call tomorrow to walk your committee through the exhibit.

Best regards,
